Where it began

Shardul Thakur was born in Palghar on 16 October 1991 and went to Swami Vivekanand International School and Junior College. He was shorter than most fast bowlers, and he had to earn his place in the Mumbai side.

His first-class debut came in November 2012, against Rajasthan at Jaipur, and the early returns were thin: four wickets in his first four matches. Then it clicked. He took 48 wickets at 20.81 in the 2014–15 Ranji Trophy, and in the 2015–16 final he claimed eight against Saurashtra as Mumbai lifted the trophy for the 41st time.

The player

A right-handed batter and right-arm seamer, he made his one-day international debut against Sri Lanka on 31 August 2017, and his first Test, against West Indies in October 2018, lasted just ten balls before an injury cut it short. He was India's 294th Test cricketer.

By November 2026 he had played 13 Tests, between 2018 and 2025, scoring 377 runs at 18.85 with four fifties and a top score of 67, and taking 33 wickets at 31.03. His best figures, 7 for 61, came at the Wanderers in January 2022, at the time the best by an Indian bowler against South Africa, and he finished that match with 8 for 108. He was also in the India squads that won the Asia Cup in 2018 and 2023.

What made him special

He had a knack of turning up when it mattered. In the famous Gabba Test against Australia he made 67 in India's first innings and picked up seven wickets across the match. At the Oval in 2021 he did it again, hitting 57 from 36 balls, his fifty coming up in 31, at the time the quickest made in any Test in England. He added 60 in the second innings and took the wickets of Ollie Pope, Rory Burns and Joe Root as India won.

Nobody would have mistaken him for the tallest bowler in the side. But he put the ball in the right place, took wickets that mattered and gave his captains runs they had not counted on.

Away from the middle

He kept busy in the Indian Premier League, starting with Kings XI Punjab and moving on to Rising Pune Supergiants, Chennai Super Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders and Lucknow Super Giants. In 2021 he was Chennai's leading wicket-taker with 21. Ahead of the 2026 season he was traded to Mumbai Indians, the franchise of the city he had long played for.

In T20 internationals he was man of the match against Sri Lanka at the 2018 Nidahas Trophy, with 4 for 27.

And finally

Plenty of seam bowlers dream of a quick fifty. Few get one faster than any Test batter had managed in England, and fewer manage it in a match they go on to help win with the ball.
